commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fix missing SwiGLU clamp in batched DeepGEMM
commits.pr_body:
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base sets `swiglu_limit=10`. Batched DeepGEMM omitted this limit in its fused SwiGLU and FP8 quantization step. With `deepep_low_latency` on 8×H200, the original code produced 9 severe token log-probability mismatches in 16,384 tokens. One token had logprob −0.31 versus −31.68 from the reference.

Apply the model's optional limit before SiLU and multiplication. Cap the gate at the upper bound and clamp the up projection to ±limit. The CUDA implementation specializes on the presence of the limit at host dispatch. The Triton kernel takes the limit as a compile-time constant. The default is `None`.

**Performance with clamp disabled.** The CUDA grid, thread count, prefetch depth, shared memory allocation and stream match upstream `ca04fba321`. All six native CUDA variants emitted byte-identical GPU instructions on both SM90 and SM100. All 452 tested unclamped Triton specializations per target also had byte-identical executable sections. SM100 code generation was checked by cross-compilation. On H200, 12 alternating rounds on each of the 25 configurations flagged by the earlier screening gave an across-configuration median of +0.01% and a range of -0.53% to +0.09% versus upstream. These timings measure GPU execution; eager dispatch and end-to-end throughput were not measured for this revision.

**Performance with clamp enabled.** On a 30-case H200 native kernel panel, enabling the required arithmetic changed latency by a median of +2.91% and a maximum of +5.46% compared with the unclamped upstream kernel (three balanced CUPTI rounds, CUDA graphs, cold L2). The panel includes FP8 scale formats, different expert loads and the model's H=2048 widths. The Triton clamp implementation retains its previously measured overhead, including +6.96% on H200 for E128/H7168 with a skewed token distribution. These figures are kernel timings.

**Correctness.** The extension was rebuilt with incremental CMake. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` passed all 110 tests. Tests compare the fused clamp with independently preclamped BF16 inputs, including zero limits, odd token counts, empty experts and padding. Pre-commit hooks passed.

At `ad9819ea79`, the Base FP8 checkpoint `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base@8855555deef230a27a21a8d6f294b7b7497759b6` ran on 8×H200 with TP1/DP8, expert parallelism, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs and `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`. All eight workers selected `BatchedDeepGemmExperts` in all 43 MoE layers with limit 10. Nine failing prefixes were replayed three times each, with zero severe mismatches. GSM8K (200 examples, five-shot, greedy, seed 1234) scored 188/200 strict and 188/200 flexible. This is a smoke evaluation. The runtime used DeepEP 2.1.0; the original report used 1.2.1.

**Other backends.** The HPC backend independently reproduced the missing clamp on the same model (34 severe mismatches in 32,563 tokens). Models requiring the limit now exclude HPC during backend selection. Explicitly forcing HPC reports the unsupported configuration. The GPU kernel and constructor for HPC retain their existing behavior.

The audit uses the original expert constructors, without the proposed model-only fallback changes. Runtime inspection checks the actual selected expert class and the clamp reaching each of 43 MoE layers in the inspected worker. Negative results mean no reproduction in these workloads, not proof that a backend is universally correct.

| Original backend | Hardware / weights | Fresh tokens / severe mismatches | Comparison |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary DeepGEMM | H200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Generated vs teacher-forced logprobs |
| Ordinary DeepGEMM FP4 | GB200 / MXFP4 | 32,692 / 0 | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS | H200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Independent H200 DeepGEMM reference |
| TRT-LLM modular FP8 | GB200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Independent H200 DeepGEMM reference |
| TRT-LLM modular MXFP4 | GB200 / MXFP4 | 32,433 / 0 | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| CuteDSL NVFP4 | GB200 / NVIDIA NVFP4 | 32,673 / 2 threshold outliers | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4 | GB200 / same NVIDIA NVFP4 | 32,766 / 1 threshold outlier | Same backend, generated vs prefill |

These deployments already forward limit=10 through the normal quantization configuration; the proposed model-only fallback changes were unnecessary for them and have been removed. The first five rows also replayed the nine original failing prefixes three times without the original severe anomaly. Same-backend prefill checks are not independent accuracy references.

CuteDSL NVFP4 correctly receives limit=10. Its two threshold outliers do not establish a missing-clamp defect: replays vary (one token scored -6.33, -9.19, -13.20), unlike the original deterministic high-confidence anomaly. The removed fallback change would pass exactly the same limit. A same-checkpoint CUTLASS control also has one threshold outlier; scoring the CuteDSL-generated tokens with CUTLASS gives three. **NVFP4 is not a clean numerical pass:** these residual differences remain unlocalized and are not claimed fixed. Neither backend receives a speculative change in this PR.

GB200 runs use TP=1/DP=2/EP on two GPUs, AG/RS communication, max length 8192. MXFP4 checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash@60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`. NVFP4 checkpoint: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4@e3cd60e7de98e9867116860d522499a728de1cf9`.

MoonEP and TRT-LLM MxInt4 have no trained-model end-to-end accuracy result in this audit and receive **no changes**. Source inspection shows MoonEP already rejects quantization-sourced clamp parameters and the normal unquantized method forwards the model limit. TRT-LLM MxInt4 does not advertise DeepSeek-V4 routing support; no suitable checkpoint was available. No ROCm/XPU correctness claim is made.

**Contribution notes.** #64976 addresses standalone SwiGLU strides/ranks and #32735 refactors the masked helper. Neither implements the missing batched MoE clamp. AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests and this description. The human submitter must review the diff and run relevant tests before merge.

commits.pr_title: [Kimi K3.1][Specialized decode] Serve GQA DSpark drafts on the specialized drafter
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Builds Kimi-K3.1's GQA sliding-window DSpark draft ([`Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark), a `Qwen3DSparkModel`) on the specialized decode's drafter under `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, as the MLA preview draft (`K3DSparkModel`) already is. On 8x B300 with the real Kimi-K3.1-Pro, the draft step drops from 751 µs to 463 µs (−38%) at TP8 and at TP8 + DCP8.

No open PR covers this (searched "specialized drafter GQA", "Kimi K3.1 DSpark specialized", "Qwen3DSpark specialized decode", "K3.1 DSpark drafter").

## Claims

- With `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, `Qwen3DSparkModel` drafts of Kimi-K3.1 are built as `SpecializedQwen3DSparkForCausalLM`; nothing changes without it.
- Draft step: 751 → 464 µs at TP8, 751 → 463 µs at TP8 + DCP8 (batch 1, k = 4).
- Full decode step at TP8 + DCP8 (the recipe's AgentX preset): 8.39 → 8.12 ms (−3.2%); the target verify (~7.2 ms) is the rest of the step.

## Validation

8x B300, real [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro), the recipe's B300 AgentX TP8 + DCP8 concurrency-1 preset (no host KV offload), `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark` with 4 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting, block rejection:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 --use-replayssm \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' --max-num-seqs 2 --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,10]}'
```

The stock drafter run is the same command on main (`8700cc9ba0`); TP8 drops the three DCP flags. Step times are from torch profiles (rank 0, 60 steps); throughput from 6 chat prompts at temperature 0, one at a time, `max_tokens=400`.

| Config | Drafter | Draft step | Target verify | Full step | Acceptance length | Output tok/s (1 stream) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 + DCP8 | stock | 751 µs | 7244 µs | 8391 µs | 3.49 | 325.7 |
| TP8 + DCP8 | this PR | 463 µs | 7271 µs | 8123 µs | 3.56 | 330.7 |
| TP8 | stock\* | 751 µs | – | – | – | – |
| TP8 | this PR | 464 µs | 7021 µs | 7844 µs | 3.62 | 350.9 |

\*Stock drafter at TP8 measured with the stock target decode (draft graph time does not depend on the target's decode backend: 751 / 759 µs with the specialized / stock target at TP8 + DCP8).

![Draft step breakdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/mgoin/pr-68701-assets/draft_step_breakdown.png)

![Decode step at TP8 + DCP8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/mgoin/pr-68701-assets/decode_step_tp8_dcp8.png)

Where the draft step's GPU time goes (µs per step, kernels summed; they overlap):

| Category | Stock | This PR | What changed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Layer GEMMs (QKV, o, MLP, context K/V, context projection) | 277 | 164 | `DraftGemm` warp split-K; context projection column-parallel |
| Markov sampling | 146 | 45 | fused, vocab-sharded Markov steps (`markov.py`) |
| Attention, norms, RoPE, KV write | 179 | 129 | eager draft forward (no torch.compile) on the same kernels; FA4 attention unchanged |
| Collectives | 112 | 110 | mailbox gather for the context projection and logits; embedding all-reduce fused with the first RMSNorm |
| LM head | 47 | 47 | the target's low-latency lm_head (unchanged) |

Output text is coherent in every run; acceptance is in line with the recipe's golden 3.19 at 4 tokens. The throughput difference is within the noise of 6 prompts; the step-time difference is the measured claim.

Checks: `pre-commit run --files vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/drafter/gqa.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/drafter/model.py` passes (ruff, mypy, docstring style).

No tests are added: CI has no Kimi-K3.1 checkpoint (the specialized decode needs the full 896-expert model and 8 SM100 GPUs), and the new class only composes the existing drafter parts, which `tests/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_specialized_decode_drafter.py` and `test_k31_drafter_comm.py` cover. The validation above is the coverage.

## Details

- `drafter/gqa.py` adds `SpecializedQwen3DSparkForCausalLM` / `SpecializedQwen3DSparkModel`, the GQA counterpart of `SpecializedK3DSparkForCausalLM`, built from the same parts: `linears.DraftGemm` for every drafter linear and the fused context K/V GEMM, `linears.draft_logits`, `markov.sample_sequential`, `comm.DrafterComm` (context-projection and logits gathers, the embedding's `ArNorm`), and `model._gathered_linear` for the column-parallel `fc`.
- The model disables `o_proj` / `down_proj` reductions and reduces them in the following RMSNorm with `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`, which the compiled stock model gets from its fusion pass; it is `@ignore_torch_compile`, like `K3DSparkModel`, since the drafter's custom kernels run in its forward.
- `drafter/model.py:register()`, which `specialized_decode_config` calls under `latency_specialized` on a Kimi-K3 target, now also registers `Qwen3DSparkModel`. It is only called in that process, so other `Qwen3DSparkModel` drafts are unaffected.
- The draft attention stays on the stock FLASH_ATTN sliding-window path (~70 µs of the step); the preview drafter's folded MLA attention does not apply to GQA.

Limitations: the remaining draft time is spread over attention (~129 µs with its norms, RoPE and KV writes), the ten all-reduce + RMSNorm sites (~73 µs) and the context projection (K = 35840 is too wide for the warp split-K, ~16 µs on cuBLAS).

## Overview

Runs GLM-5.3-Flash's block-FP8 routed and shared experts in DeepGEMM Mega MoE on SM90 (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on H200), through a new weight format `MEGA_MOE_FP8_BLOCK_SM90`. The checkpoint's E4M3 weights and FP32 128x128 block scales go to the kernel without MXFP8 requantization. SM100 keeps `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8`. Builds on the GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE path of #60895.

Pins DeepGEMM to vllm-project/DeepGEMM `dev` [`44cba7d`](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/44cba7d28066182852005c59052f035ebc18e211), the merge of vllm-project/DeepGEMM#57 on top of main's pin.

## Claims

- At default memory on 8x H200, Mega MoE leads both main backends (default and FI MoE-EP) at every measured point, with the largest KV pool: 66.44 GiB per GPU against 60.12 (FI MoE-EP) and 54.05 (main default). On 4x H200 it leads FI MoE-EP and DeepEP v2 at every point; main default ran out of memory there once (Limitations).
- On the AgentX sweep from c=1 to c=256, Mega MoE beats main's default MoE at every level on 4x and 8x H200 in output tok/s per GPU (+12% to +24% at c=1..32), and per user everywhere except c=128 on 4x H200 (-12%, inside the noise). Per-user speed is +26% to +34% at c=1..32.
- Mega MoE leaves more memory for the KV cache at the same memory setting: 3.1-4.4 GiB more per GPU at DP4 (11-16.5% more KV tokens), 6.3-12.4 GiB more at DP8 (10.5-22.9%). This is part of the feature and gives most of the lead over FI MoE-EP at AgentX c=64.
- At an equal 24 GiB KV pool (DP4), AgentX is +12% (c=16) and +16% (c=64) over main's default MoE. Against FI MoE-EP it is +10.5% at c=16 and -2.1% at c=64, where the pool is the limit.
- GSM8K, paired per question, shows no difference to main's default MoE; logprobs are as close to main default as FI MoE-EP's are.

## Validation

```
  --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --max-model-len 142000 \
  --disable-extensible-kv-cache --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  <arm flag>
```

| Mega MoE (this PR) | `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` |
| FI MoE-EP (#62603) | `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` |
| DeepEP v2 | `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` (DEEPGEMM FP8 experts) |
| main default | none (FLASHINFER_CUTLASS + `allgather_reducescatter`) |

Random: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`, `d` = 1k in / 1k out, `p` = 8k in / 256 out, prompts max(32, 4c), prefix cache reset per point. AgentX: agentic-coding trace replay, 900 s per level. Output tok/s is for the whole server. Single runs unless stated.

The tables were measured on main `f48bfde4d` with this PR's code as of `89f5229e2` and DeepGEMM `a49ea3f`, before the rebase onto `191e5d5df`. Sanity runs of Mega MoE at DP4 default memory on the rebased code matched:

### Blackwell (SM100)

**Loading.** `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` picks the SM90 format on SM90 and rejects block sizes other than 128x128. Weights load straight into the kernel layout; block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`. The kernel scales `*_weight_scale` are registered at construction in their final layout (FP32, MN-major, MN stride padded to a multiple of 4). `finalize_block_fp8_weights` lays them out with DeepGEMM's `transform_fp8_block_sf_for_sm90_mega_moe` (through a wrapper in `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) and copies them in place, so the storage CUDA graphs captured stays valid across layerwise and direct reloads. **Routing.** GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE routes with `fused_grouped_topk` (one group, sigmoid scoring), as Kimi K3 Mega MoE does, instead of `fused_topk_bias`, and checks at init for sigmoid scoring with a correction bias. On 200k random router rows both pick the same experts (max relative weight difference 4e-7). End to end on 4x H200 (KV 24 GiB, random 1k/1k, `fused_grouped_topk` run twice), it gives +3.1% output tok/s at c=1 (mean ITL 9.16 against 9.45 ms) and +2.1% at c=16; +0.6% at c=64 and +0.3% at c=256 are within the 0.1-1.0% spread between the two runs. GSM8K shows no difference. `fused_grouped_topk` is called without the router-side padding mask, so capture hooks see real expert ids on padded rows.

**Warmup.** The DeepGEMM Mega MoE warmup now covers `Glm5NextMoE` on every GPU and weight format.

**Guards.** EPLB's expert view now accepts the padded SM90 block-scale layout, and `check_deep_gemm_mega_moe_supported` rejects SM90-only formats on SM100; neither case is reachable for GLM today. Two tests cover them.

**Docs.** The `deep_gemm_mega_moe` entry of the `moe_backend` docstring (`vllm/config/kernel.py`) now lists the supported experts per GPU: MXFP4, MXFP8, NVFP4 or BF16 on SM100, MXFP4 or 128x128 block-FP8 on SM90. The GLM-5.3-Flash recipe gets an `h200_dep_mega_moe` preset (FP8, DP + EP, opt-in) with a guide section. It is text-only for now because H200 DP with image and video input on hits an illegal memory access in encoder profiling, on main too. On 8x H200 the rendered DP8 command comes up with the default `--max-num-seqs` and scores 0.97 on the first 100 GSM8K questions; on 4x H200 it needs `--max-num-seqs 948`.

**CI.** The GLM5Next H200 job also triggers on `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`. `test_reload_requantizes_into_the_kernel_tensors` runs SM90 × {layerwise, direct} reload. The H100 DeepGEMM Kernels job now runs `test_deep_gemm_warmup.py`, which mocks every DeepGEMM call. The SM90 cases of `test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (#64061's MXFP4 cases and this PR's block-FP8 case) run in no CI job, because the file runs only on B200. They were run on H200.

**Not a duplicate of #62603.** #62603 (merged) added a separate opt-in backend on FlashInfer's MoE-EP CuTe DSL kernels and does not fuse the shared expert. This PR adds a weight format to the existing DeepGEMM Mega MoE backend, with the shared expert fused in the launch. Both are measured above.

**Limitations.**
- SM90 needs 128x128 block-FP8 checkpoints. BF16 GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE stays SM100-only.
- EP with TP=1 and one expert group, as on SM100. TP2xDP2+EP4 cannot use Mega MoE.
- `--all2all-backend` is ignored when Mega MoE is selected (as before).
- Main's default MoE backend ran out of memory at DP4+EP4 default memory, 40 s into GSM8K (FlashInfer CUTLASS asked for 4.88 GiB with 4.02 GiB free; seen once, and not at DP8+EP8). It is the failure mode of #60471 (FlashInfer CUTLASS workspace OOM after profiling; proposed fix #60570), on main and not caused by this PR.

## Overview

Add `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` support for `Lfm3VlForConditionalGeneration` (`LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B`) across image and video inputs. Related to #38175.

Because `Lfm3VlVisionModel` interleaves attention with 2D depthwise convolutions (`Lfm3VlVisionConv2d`) over variable native-resolution `(H, W)` grids, we precompute 1-based spatial neighbor indices (`conv_indices`) outside the graph and run a fused Triton gather-conv2d kernel inside the graph so arbitrary aspect ratios share one 1D token-budget graph set.

## Claims

- Image, multi-image, and video encoder CUDA Graph support for `LFM3-VL` (`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`), leaving the default eager path (`cudagraph_mm_encoder=False`) unchanged.
- **27.3% lower Mean TTFT** (`53.02 → 38.55 ms`) and **40.7% lower P99 TTFT** (`111.10 → 65.90 ms`) on `LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B` (RTX 5070 Ti, BF16, 2 images/req @ 8 RPS).
- Exact encoder output parity on tested image budgets (`max_abs_error = 0.0`) and no accuracy degradation on MMStar (`56.67% → 57.50%`).

## Validation

```bash
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \

# -> Passed
```

### E2E serving performance (`vllm bench serve`)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Don't pin the grammar bitmask
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #67335, `allocate_token_bitmask` pins the structured-output bitmask, and #68484 removed the unpinned fallback. In EngineCore, pinning creates a CUDA context on the first structured-output request. When that fails, EngineCore dies and the server goes down with it. This PR allocates the bitmask unpinned, as the default xgrammar backend did before #67335.

## Claims

- The grammar bitmask is allocated unpinned, so the first structured-output request no longer creates a CUDA context in EngineCore.

## Validation

I hit this once on two GB10 nodes (TP=2, `mp` executor) at a87e3a6554 plus unrelated patches, with xgrammar 0.2.9 and the Rust frontend. The first `response_format` `json_schema` request killed EngineCore. The same image passed that request on two other loads. The Python frontend reaches the same EngineCore call.

<details>
<summary>EngineCore log</summary>

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 803, in step_with_batch_queue
    grammar_output = self.scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 2296, in get_grammar_bitmask
    bitmask = self.structured_output_manager.grammar_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py", line 396, in grammar_bitmask
    self._grammar_bitmask = allocate_token_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py", line 59, in allocate_token_bitmask
    return torch.full(
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
The CUDA driver logged these messages, which may provide useful details:
Returning 2 (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) from cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain
```

</details>

On d33bfeef40 (macOS, CPU), the new test fails on main and passes with this PR. It sets `PIN_MEMORY` and makes pinned allocation raise the error above:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS=none HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest -q --durations=0 --durations-min=0 tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py -k does_not_pin
```

main:
```
vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py:59: in allocate_token_bitmask
E           torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
FAILED tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py::test_allocate_token_bitmask_does_not_pin
1 failed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 0.13s
```

PR (4ab3601807):
```
0.00s call     tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py::test_allocate_token_bitmask_does_not_pin
1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 0.13s
```

`tests/v1/structured_output` has the same failures on main and on this PR apart from the new test. They come from my offline Mac setup (tokenizers missing from the HF cache, no Triton). CI runs the suite in `(CPU) V1 Others`. `tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py` passes on both (66 passed). pre-commit passes.

## Details

- Root cause: the scheduler fills the bitmask on the CPU and puts `.numpy()` into `GrammarOutput`. `MultiprocExecutor` pickles it to the workers, where `StructuredOutputsWorker.apply_grammar_bitmask` copies it with `async_tensor_h2d`, which stages unpinned input through pinned memory. Pinning in EngineCore therefore saves nothing and only creates a CUDA context there. On GB10 that context creation failed in `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain`.
- With `UniProcExecutor`, `async_tensor_h2d` now stages the used rows once per step, as it did for xgrammar before #67335 (`xgr.allocate_token_bitmask` does not pin).
- This keeps #68484's approach of not falling back: the bitmask is not pinned at all. The other caller, offline beam search, also reads the bitmask only on the CPU.
- No `LLM`-level test: CI GPUs can create the context, so the crash needs a failing context creation, which the unit test emulates.
- Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR on this (searched `allocate_token_bitmask`, pinned bitmask, structured-output CUDA OOM, follow-ups to #67335 and #68484).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix MXFP8 linear layers whose N is not a multiple of 8 or 32
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The FlashInfer MXFP8 linear kernels compute garbage or fail when a layer's N is not a multiple of 8 (CuTe-DSL) or 32 (CUTLASS). Split out of #67941, which now has only its unrelated KV cache layout fix.

## Claims

- The CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS MXFP8 linear kernels pad N with zero rows to a multiple of 8 and 32, and slice their output back to the layer's N. On `main`, CuTe-DSL wrote `inf` or garbage for such layers at M = 64, and CUTLASS raised.
- Kernel selection is unchanged, and layers with aligned N run as before.

## Validation

One node of 4x GB300 (SM103), torch 2.14, FlashInfer `main`, vLLM's compiled extensions from the wheel of `main` `26acafd`.

**The new tests** (`tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_unaligned_n.py`, both kernels at N = 130, 1036, 1048, 2064, 4608 and M = 1, 64, plus whichever kernel vLLM selects at N = 1036, 2072), against the dequantized reference:

- On `main`: **11 failed, 13 passed**. CUTLASS raises for every N not a multiple of 32, and CuTe-DSL is off at M = 64 for N not a multiple of 8 (M = 1 happens to come out right on its low-M split-K path):

```
RuntimeError: Check failed: n % alignment == 0 (2 vs. 0) : Expected n to be divisible by 32, but got mat2 shape: (130x256).
```

- With this PR: **24 passed**.

**Other tests that use these kernels**, run on `main` and with this PR: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py`, `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`, `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py`, `tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_encoder_autotune.py` and `tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py`, `test_numerics.py`. This PR adds no failures; the same 25 fail on both (24 `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases, whose test layers lack `params_dtype`, and `test_specialized_decode_numerics`, which needs `ray`).

**CI:** the B200 Kernels step in `kernels.yaml` now runs `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_unaligned_n.py` and `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`; both skip on GPUs other than SM100.

**pre-commit** on the changed files: ruff, typos, mypy and the repo's own checks pass (the markdown, shell, GitHub Actions, C++, Rust and requirements hooks were skipped: no such files changed).

## Details

FlashInfer's CuTe-DSL MXFP8 GEMM stores its bf16/fp16 output with TMA, which needs 16-byte aligned rows (N % 8 == 0). `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel.can_implement` checks only `mm_mxfp8`'s generic limits (K ≥ 128, K % 32 == 0, N ≥ 128), so it takes such layers, and FlashInfer launched its untuned fallback tactic, which wrote garbage: at N = 130, K = 256, M = 64, a relative RMS error of 17.5 against the dequantized reference. M = 1 comes out right, so a single decode shows nothing. `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` needs N % 32 == 0 and neither checked nor padded it.

Both kernels now pad N in `process_weights_after_loading` with zero weight rows and scales (`_pad_n`: at most 7 or 31 extra rows per such layer, logged once per shape) and slice the GEMM output back to `output_size_per_partition`, copying it so that it stays contiguous. Layers whose N needs no padding are neither padded nor copied. The TRT-LLM kernel's existing padding to a multiple of 128 uses the same helper.

Not covered: SM120 keeps its existing N % 32 check.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't let later image requests overtake a request deferred for encoder limits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #67292. With chunked prefill off and async scheduling, a multimodal request that the scheduler defers whole for encoder cache or budget limits (#65399) can be skipped indefinitely, while later requests with fewer images take the encoder cache space it needs.

With this PR, once the scheduler defers a request this way, it admits no later request that needs encoder output in that step, as long as the deferred request's images fit the configured encoder cache at once. In the issue's repro, the 4-image request is then scheduled whole at step 2, where before it was not scheduled in 50 steps.

## Claims

- Under FCFS, with chunked prefill off and async scheduling or pipeline parallelism, a request deferred for encoder limits is no longer overtaken by later requests that need encoder output, provided the embeddings of all its images add up to no more than the configured encoder cache size. It is scheduled whole once the steps in flight at the deferral have been processed, with one exception described in Details.
- In the scheduler-only repro from #67292, with `AsyncScheduler` and chunked prefill off, the 4-image request is scheduled whole at step 2. Before this change it was not scheduled in 50 steps.
- On `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` served with chunked prefill off and async scheduling under a sustained one-image load, base completed none of the 4-image requests within 30 s in any of its saturated runs, and the first version of this change completed all of them, with a median time to first token of 0.45 to 1.36 s. This includes one-image requests with `max_tokens=1`, the prefill-only and scoring case.
- Both ways the encoder step defers a request are covered. It can cut the request at the start of an image that begins after its first uncomputed token (#65399's deferral), or cut it to zero tokens because the image at its first uncomputed token does not fit.
- Later requests are not held when their tokens in the step include no image embeddings, or when the deferred request's images can't all fit the configured encoder cache at once.
- Chunked prefill on, encoder-only and encoder-decoder models, and synchronous scheduling without pipeline parallelism are unchanged.

## Validation

The unit tests ran on one H100 machine from a source tree at main (`0db6f1ba5`) with the compiled extensions of the `c02ebf136` precompiled wheel (main has no compiled-code changes since then). The CUDA runs had one GPU visible. The CPU runs had none and set `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py` passes at main's hook pins, including ruff, mypy, typos, the docstring style check and the test-tethering check.

### Tests

Four tests are added to `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, next to the test from #65399, and `create_scheduler` gains an `encoder_cache_size` argument. The tests build their scheduler with one helper, `_encoder_deferral_scheduler`, which calls `create_scheduler(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf", max_num_batched_tokens=1024, ...)` with chunked prefill off by default. The encoder cache and budget are then 1,024 embeddings, except in the test that sets `encoder_cache_size`. CI runs this file only on the CPU platform, where `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config` turns async scheduling off, so the helper sets the requested `async_scheduling` back on the scheduler's config after construction. State built during construction still follows the platform. The helper asserts that the async cases see overlapping batches (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`) and the sync case does not. The new tests are in a `cpu_test` file that the `pytest -v -s -m 'cpu_test' v1/core` step of the CPU CI job runs.

<details>
<summary>What each new test sets up and checks</summary>

- `test_encoder_deferred_request_is_not_overtaken` is the scenario from #67292. Three one-image requests (250 embeddings each) are in flight, a 1,020-token request arrives, and two more one-image requests arrive before every step. In the `async` case the request has 4 images (1,000 embeddings) and is cut before its second one. In the `async-cut-to-zero` case it has one 800-embedding image at token 0 and is cut to zero tokens. Both must be scheduled whole at step 2. The `sync` case (whole at step 1) and the `chunked-prefill` case (first 260 tokens at step 1) are controls that pass before and after the change.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_later_requests_needing_the_encoder` checks a single step. While `deferred` waits for encoder cache space, a one-image request that would fit in the 424 free slots waits too, and a text-only request and a request whose image is in its prefix-cache hit are scheduled.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_requests_with_embeddings_in_window` checks the two steps after `busy` is scheduled. Three 800-token requests each get 512 tokens from a mocked KV connector, and `tail`'s 600-token image has 400 embeddings. While `deferred` waits for 600 slots with 424 free, `tail` is scheduled when its remaining 288 tokens overlap the image only at positions without embeddings (at image offsets 0 and 40), and waits when they include embeddings. Once the first step is processed, `deferred` is scheduled in every case.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_behind_requests_fitting_the_encoder_cache` sets a 600-embedding encoder cache, of which an in-flight request holds 300. A deferred request with two 300-embedding images exactly fits the cache, holds a later one-image request, and is scheduled once the in-flight step is processed. One with two 400-embedding images never fits, and the later request is scheduled.

</details>

Six cases fail with main's `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`. In the `async` and `async-cut-to-zero` cases the deferred request is not scheduled in 8 steps, which is the reported bug. In `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_later_requests_needing_the_encoder` and the `embeds-in-window`, `embeds-in-window-offset` and `fits-cache` cases, main schedules the later request. The three cases where a later request must not be held (`no-embeds-in-window`, `no-embeds-in-window-offset` and `never-fits-cache`) fail with this PR's first commit (`fe59ae11f`), which held it. ### End to end

End to end, the starvation and the fix both reproduce on `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, served with the first version of this change applied to `3bc0f4308` on one H100. Base is `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` at `3bc0f4308`. `scheduler.py` on main has changed since that commit, and the end-to-end runs were not repeated after the rebases or the review changes. I expect the review changes not to affect them, because the runs had no prefix-cache hits, so every request was scheduled whole with all of its images' embeddings in the step, and every request's images (at most 1,120 embeddings) fit the 1,280-embedding encoder cache at once.

```text
vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18013 \
    --max-model-len 1280 --max-num-batched-tokens 1280 \
    --no-enable-chunked-prefill --async-scheduling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "audio": 0, "video": 0}'
```

These settings make the scheduler's encoder cache and per-step encoder budget 1,280 embeddings (the engine logs `Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 1280 tokens`). `--max-model-len 1280` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 1280` were chosen to make the cache tight, and these runs do not measure how often the condition arises with a larger cache. Each image is a distinct 160x112 random-noise JPEG, which Gemma 4 turns into 280 embeddings, so a 4-image request (1,151 prompt tokens, 1,120 embeddings) fits only when the previous step admitted no one-image request. The load client sends one-image chat requests and, every 5 s from 5 s to 60 s of a 90 s run, a 4-image request with `max_tokens=1`, so a 4-image request's latency is its time to first token. Each 4-image request has a 30 s timeout, and the tables count a request as done only if it returned within 30 s.

<details>
<summary>The one-image requests, and how servers and image seeds were reused</summary>

The one-image chat requests have 298 or 379 prompt tokens, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=1` or `max_tokens=8` (with `max_tokens=8` they generated about 4 tokens each). Every run uses images that no other request on that server has used. Open-loop runs, the same-node pairs and the iteration-logging run each start a fresh server. In the other closed-loop jobs the 32-client run follows the 16-client run on the same server with a new image seed base, and the server log shows a 0.0% prefix cache hit rate throughout. Each configuration ran once, apart from 22 one-image requests per second and 379 tokens at 16 clients with `max_tokens=8`.

</details>

With a sustained backlog (closed loop, where each of 16 or 32 clients sends its next one-image request as soon as the previous one returns), base starves the 4-image requests and the change serves all of them. This holds when the one-image requests generate a single token, as prefill-only and scoring workloads do, and when they generate several. """Open-loop load on a vLLM OpenAI server: one-image requests at a fixed rate plus a 4-image request every
```python
--big-every seconds. Every image is distinct random noise of 160x112 pixels (280 Gemma 4 soft tokens), so the
encoder cache never hits. A request that has not finished within its timeout is cancelled and counted as such.

    load.py --port P (--rate R | --concurrency C) [--duration 90] [--big-every 5] [--big-until 60] --out result.json

With --concurrency C, one-image requests are closed-loop instead: C clients each send the next one-image request as
soon as their previous one finishes, until --duration.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import base64
import io
import json
import time

import aiohttp
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

MODEL = "google/gemma-4-E2B-it"


def image_url(seed: int) -> str:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 256, (112, 160, 3), dtype=np.uint8)).save(buf, format="JPEG", quality=90)
    return "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()


def payload(seeds: list[int], text: str, max_tokens: int) -> dict:
    content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_url(s)}} for s in seeds]
    content.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
    return {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}], "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": 0}


async def send(session, url, kind, idx, body, t0, timeout, results):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    rec = {"kind": kind, "idx": idx, "sent": round(start - t0, 4)}
    try:
        async with session.post(url, json=body, timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout)) as r:
            data = await r.json(content_type=None)
            rec["status"] = r.status
            if r.status == 200:
                rec["prompt_tokens"] = data["usage"]["prompt_tokens"]
                rec["completion_tokens"] = data["usage"]["completion_tokens"]
            else:
                rec["error"] = str(data)[:300]
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        rec["status"] = "timeout"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        rec["status"] = "error"
        rec["error"] = repr(e)[:300]
    rec["latency"] = round(time.perf_counter() - start, 4)
    results.append(rec)


def pct(xs, q):
    if not xs:
        return None
    xs = sorted(xs)
    return round(xs[min(len(xs) - 1, int(q * len(xs)))], 3)


async def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=0.0, help="open-loop one-image requests per second")
    ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=0, help="closed-loop one-image clients")
    ap.add_argument("--duration", type=float, default=90.0)
    ap.add_argument("--big-every", type=float, default=5.0)
    ap.add_argument("--big-until", type=float, default=60.0)
    ap.add_argument("--big-timeout", type=float, default=30.0)
    ap.add_argument("--small-timeout", type=float, default=60.0)
    ap.add_argument("--small-max-tokens", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--small-words", type=int, default=0, help="filler words appended to the one-image prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--seed-base", type=int, default=None,
                    help="offset for all image seeds; defaults to a time-based value so runs never repeat an image")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{a.port}/v1/chat/completions"
    sb = a.seed_base if a.seed_base is not None else (time.time_ns() // 1000) % 10**12 * 10**10
    small_text, big_text = "Describe the image in one word.", "Which of the four images is brightest? Answer 1-4."
    filler = "Consider the colours, textures and shapes in the picture carefully before you answer.".split()
    if a.small_words:
        small_text += " " + " ".join(filler[k % len(filler)] for k in range(a.small_words))

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0)) as session:
        # Warm-up and token check, one request at a time, distinct seeds from the load.
        warm = []
        for kind, seeds, text, mt in (("small", [sb + 10**9], small_text, a.small_max_tokens),
                                      ("big", [sb + 10**9 + i for i in range(1, 5)], big_text, 1)):
            await send(session, url, kind, -1, payload(seeds, text, mt), time.perf_counter(), 120, warm)
        print("warm-up:", json.dumps(warm))

        n_small = 0 if a.concurrency else int(a.rate * a.duration)
        big_times = [a.big_every * j for j in range(1, int(a.big_until / a.big_every) + 1)]
        events = [(i / a.rate, "small", i) for i in range(n_small)] + [(t, "big", j) for j, t in enumerate(big_times)]
        events.sort()
        bodies = {}
        for _, kind, i in events:
            if kind == "small":
                bodies[(kind, i)] = payload([sb + i], small_text, a.small_max_tokens)
            else:
                bodies[(kind, i)] = payload([sb + 5 * 10**8 + 4 * i + k for k in range(4)], big_text, 1)
        results, tasks, lag = [], [], 0.0
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        counter = iter(range(10**8))

        async def closed_loop_client():
            while time.perf_counter() - t0 < a.duration:
                i = next(counter)
                await send(session, url, "small", i, payload([sb + i], small_text, a.small_max_tokens), t0,
                           a.small_timeout, results)

        tasks += [asyncio.create_task(closed_loop_client()) for _ in range(a.concurrency)]
        for t, kind, i in events:
            delay = t0 + t - time.perf_counter()
            if delay > 0:
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            else:
                lag = max(lag, -delay)
            timeout = a.big_timeout if kind == "big" else a.small_timeout
            tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(send(session, url, kind, i, bodies[(kind, i)], t0, timeout, results)))
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

    big = [r for r in results if r["kind"] == "big"]
    small = [r for r in results if r["kind"] == "small"]
    big_ok = [r["latency"] for r in big if r["status"] == 200]
    small_ok = [r for r in small if r["status"] == 200]
    in_window = [r for r in small_ok if r["sent"] + r["latency"] <= a.duration]
    summary = {
        "rate": a.rate, "concurrency": a.concurrency, "small_words": a.small_words, "seed_base": sb, "duration": a.duration, "max_send_lag_s": round(lag, 3),
        "big": {"sent": len(big), "completed": len(big_ok), "timed_out": sum(r["status"] == "timeout" for r in big),
                "errors": sum(r["status"] not in (200, "timeout") for r in big),
                "latency_p50": pct(big_ok, 0.5), "latency_max": pct(big_ok, 1.0),
                "latencies": sorted(round(x, 2) for x in big_ok)},
        "small": {"sent": len(small), "completed": len(small_ok),
                  "timed_out": sum(r["status"] == "timeout" for r in small),
                  "errors": sum(r["status"] not in (200, "timeout") for r in small),
                  "completed_per_s_in_window": round(len(in_window) / a.duration, 2),
                  "latency_p50": pct([r["latency"] for r in small_ok], 0.5),
                  "latency_p99": pct([r["latency"] for r in small_ok], 0.99)},
        "prompt_tokens": sorted({(r["kind"], r.get("prompt_tokens")) for r in results if r["status"] == 200}),
        "first_errors": [r for r in results if r["status"] not in (200, "timeout")][:3],
    }
    json.dump({"summary": summary, "warmup": warm, "requests": sorted(results, key=lambda r: r["sent"])},
              open(a.out, "w"))
    print(json.dumps(summary))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>A scheduler-only simulation of the server runs, which reproduces the 379-token results but not the 298-token starvation</summary>

A scheduler-only simulation with the server's settings (`AsyncScheduler`, encoder cache, encoder budget and token budget of 1,280, 280-embedding images, a 4-image request every 60 steps, 600 steps), run with the first version of this change and not repeated since, reproduces the 379-token results. With 379-token one-image requests at 16 or 32 clients, base never schedules a 4-image request, whether the one-image requests decode 1 or 4 tokens. The change schedules each one 5 or 13 steps after it arrives with 4-token decodes, and 8 or 16 steps with 1-token decodes.

It does not reproduce the server's 298-token starvation. With 298-token requests the simulated base schedules every 4-image request within 16 steps at 16 and 32 clients, because all simulated clients start in the same step and steps then alternate between four new one-image requests and none. I assume the server's staggered arrivals prevent that pattern (the server's 10-second stats samples under load in the 298-token `max_tokens=1` base run show 1 or 3 requests running) but did not test it. With 8 clients, base and the change both schedule every 4-image request within 5 steps.

</details>

There is no `LLM`-level regression test, because whether a request is overtaken depends on how steps overlap under async scheduling and on the arrival pattern, which a serving test cannot control reliably.

## Details

### Root cause

The root cause is in how async scheduling meets the whole-request deferral. Step t is planned before step t-1's output is processed, and encoder cache entries are released only in `update_from_output`. When the deferred request is checked, the previous step's entries still hold their space, so it fails `can_allocate` for one of its images and is skipped whole. The loop then admits later requests whose fewer images fit in the space left, and those requests hold that space when the deferred request is checked at the next step. This repeats as long as every step admits another image request.

### The change

`schedule()` now sets a step-local flag when `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` cuts a request's tokens and all of that request's images fit the configured encoder cache at once. It does so only if chunked prefill is off, batches overlap (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`, that is async scheduling or pipeline parallelism), and the model is neither encoder-only nor encoder-decoder. A request rejected for an encoder embedding-count mismatch does not set the flag, so a run of such requests is still rejected in one step. Without chunked prefill, every cut ends in a skip in the same iteration, through #65399's branch or the existing `num_new_tokens == 0` path, so no request that sets the flag is admitted.

For the rest of that step, the scheduler checks each later waiting request before calling `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs`. If the window that call would examine includes embeddings of one of the request's images, the request is requeued with `skip_request`, so it takes no encoder cache references and evicts nothing. The check finds the images in the window with `get_mm_features_in_window`, and counts their embeddings there with `PlaceholderRange.get_embeds_indices_in_range`, as `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` does. Text-only requests, requests whose images are all inside their prefix-cache hit, and requests whose remaining tokens overlap an image only at placeholder positions that are not embeddings are therefore not held.

### Why the deferred request gets through

Under FCFS, no later request allocates encoder space in the step of the deferral, and `skip_request` puts the deferred request back at the head of the waiting queue. Once the steps in flight at the deferral have been processed (one step with async scheduling, more with pipeline parallelism, which no test here covers), its images compete only with requests ahead of it.

With chunked prefill off and the default encoder cache size, every decoder-only request's images fit the encoder cache and budget at once, and with a configured size the flag is set only behind a request whose images do. With the built-in `EncoderCacheManager`, the deferred request therefore fits once the steps in flight are processed, and the flag cannot hold later requests indefinitely.

<details>
<summary>Why every request's images fit at the default size</summary>

With chunked prefill off, `SchedulerConfig` requires `max_num_batched_tokens >= max_model_len`, sets the encoder budget to `max_num_batched_tokens`, and sets the encoder cache size to it unless `--encoder-cache-size` (#65534) is given. `compute_mm_encoder_budget` only raises both. A decoder-only request's embeddings are at most its placeholder tokens, which are at most its prompt tokens, which are fewer than `max_model_len`. So with the default size every request's images fit the encoder cache and budget at once.

</details>

The exception is a later request that needs no embeddings in the step but whose image is already cached. It is not held, takes a reference, and can keep that entry from the deferred request for one more step. Under the priority policy, and for requests scanned before the waiting queue (`kv_holding_waiting`, an older `async_kv_waiting` head, or requests moved ahead by cache-aware admission), the deferred request can still be preceded, and later requests that need embeddings wait with it while it stays deferred.

### Costs and limits

The rule has costs. Later requests that need embeddings wait until the deferred request is admitted, even when they would fit, so a step where only image requests are waiting schedules nothing. Step 1 of the repro is such a step. In the end-to-end runs above this cost nothing measurable up to 18 one-image requests per second. At 22 per second the one-image median latency was higher with the change in all three pairs, by 0.09 s in the pair run on one node and by 0.33 and 0.44 s in the two cross-node pairs. Under saturation the one-image p99 was higher in all nine pairs (0.02 to 0.36 s).

A later request whose tokens include embeddings of an image that is already in the encoder cache also waits, because taking a reference pins an entry that the deferred request may need to evict. A later request whose tokens overlap its images only at positions without embeddings is not held, and goes through `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` as on main. That method checks cache space before it finds that no embeddings are needed. In a tight cache such a request is therefore still cut to zero tokens as on main, and if its image is in the encoder cache it takes a reference to it, which keeps that entry from the deferred request until the step is processed. I checked the tight-cache case separately with 324 free slots, where nothing is scheduled on main or with this PR. No test covers it.

<details>
<summary>Why the flag needs overlapping batches and a decoder-only model</summary>

The flag is only set when batches overlap, because with a single synchronous stage every entry is released before the next step, a deferred request is not overtaken, and holding later requests would only delay them. Encoder-decoder models are left out because their encoder input is not part of the decoder prompt, so the sizing argument above does not cover them, and #65399's deferral never applied to them.

</details>

A request whose images can't all fit the configured encoder cache (`--encoder-cache-size`, #65534) at once does not set the flag. With chunked prefill off it can wait forever, on main and with this PR, and the hold behind it would last as long. The check counts all of the request's images, including repeated ones and any inside its prefix-cache hit, against the configured size, which the built-in manager may raise to the largest item, so it can leave the flag unset for a request that would fit.

### Possible follow-ups

Three refinements are possible as follow-ups: reserving encoder cache space for the deferred request, rejecting at admission a request whose images can never fit, and looking for embeddings before the encoder cache lookup.

<details>
<summary>The three follow-ups in more detail</summary>

- The scheduler could reserve encoder cache space for the deferred request instead of holding every later request that needs embeddings. It would record the deferred request's uncached encoder need and admit later requests only while this step's allocations leave that much room at the next step. That avoids idle steps when the cache is not tight, at the cost of more scheduler state.
- The scheduler could reject at admission a request whose images can never fit the encoder cache or budget at once, as #67292 also suggests. With chunked prefill off this happens when `--encoder-cache-size` is below a request's embeddings, and such a request can then wait forever, without holding others.
- `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` could look for embeddings in the window before the cache lookup and the space check, so that a request needing none of an image's embeddings is not cut in a tight cache and takes no reference to the cached image. That changes admission for every configuration, chunked prefill on included.

</details>

### Not a duplicate

This does not duplicate an open PR. Searches of open PRs on 2026-11-12 for `67292 in:body`, "encoder cache deferred scheduler starvation", "encoder budget starvation", "skip_request encoder cache", "overtake encoder" and "encoder cache chunked prefill disabled multimodal scheduler" found nothing that changes which requests are admitted after an encoder deferral. The closest are #61733, which rejects prompts longer than the token budget when chunked prefill is off, #62030, which validates `long_prefill_token_threshold` against the largest multimodal item, and #62348, which adds metrics for deferred waiting requests. GoyalIshaan offered on the issue on 2026-11-12 to work on this fix, and no PR from them was open that day. Searches on 2026-11-16 for `67292`, "encoder deferral" and "encoder cache starvation" found only this PR.

commits.pr_body:
Fixes #67197

### Motivation & Security Impact
Previously, `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` accepted arbitrarily long inputs without enforcing an upper bound, exposing the API server to CPU exhaustion and OOM/DoS risks from oversized payloads.

This PR introduces `--max-tokenize-tokens` (defaulting to `max(max_model_len * 2, 131072)`) to reject oversized requests with HTTP 400 across both standard template rendering and GPT-OSS Harmony rendering paths, and explicitly marks both the CLI flag and environment variable as unsupported in the Rust frontend so it fails loudly on startup.

### Summary
- **CLI & Env Var Configuration:** Added `--max-tokenize-tokens` CLI flag and `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` env var (CLI takes precedence; blank/whitespace env vars are safely treated as unset; excluded from `torch.compile` cache `ignored_factors`).
- **Endpoint & Renderer Enforcement:** Applied the token limit (including early character-length pre-checks) to `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` across both standard template rendering and GPT-OSS Harmony rendering (`OnlineRenderer._make_request_with_harmony` when `tok_params` is provided).
- **Default & Opt-out Behavior:** Defaults to `max(max_model_len * 2, 131072)`; set `<= 0` to disable.
- **Rust Frontend Guard:** Added `max_tokenize_tokens` to `ServerUnsupportedArgs` in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs` so passing either the CLI flag or `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` fails loudly on startup instead of silently ignoring the limit.
- **Tests:** Added unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_max_tokenize_tokens.py` covering CLI/env precedence, blank env vars, default ceiling/floor, over-limit rejection, and Harmony rendering behavior.

## Overview

vLLM's dense JIT warmup for FlashAttention 4 (FA4), registered for Gemma 4 checkpoints, compiles the SplitKV combine kernel of the SM90 head-size-512 forward for one query head. FA4 keys that kernel on the number of heads, so the warmed kernel matches no layer, and the first split-KV call for each head count and split bucket compiles the combine while serving.

This PR adds the layer's query heads to the warmup's compile key and compiles the combine for them. On H100 with stock Gemma 4 in the default CUDA graph mode, the first request that adds 64 tokens to a cached 32K-token prompt takes 0.074 s instead of 0.534 s on E2B, and 0.069 s instead of 0.507 s on 12B.

## Claims

- On H100 with stock `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and `google/gemma-4-12B-it` in the default CUDA graph mode, the first request that adds 64 tokens to a cached 32K-token prompt takes 0.534 s on main and 0.074 s with this PR on E2B, and 0.507 s and 0.069 s on 12B. The next such request takes 0.051 to 0.061 s on both builds.
- On main, that first request adds one kernel to FA4's combine cache, at head size 512 with the layer's 8 (E2B) or 16 (12B) query heads. With this PR it adds none. Neither build compiles a forward kernel in these requests.
- A fresh 32K-token prompt doesn't split the keys and takes the same time on both builds (0.441 and 0.435 s on E2B, 1.651 and 1.661 s on 12B).
- The JIT warmup took 9.84 s on main and 10.06 s with this PR on E2B, and 11.71 s and 11.10 s on 12B.

## Validation

All runs are on H100 80GB with main `c02ebf136e`, torch 2.14.0+cu130 and flash-attention `8dd9eaea`. `c02ebf136e` has no precompiled wheel yet, so the binaries come from its parent `777288d2eb`'s wheel. No file in `csrc/`, `cmake/`, `requirements/` or `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/` differs between the two, and neither do `CMakeLists.txt` and `setup.py`.

| Command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_fa4_dense_warmup.py` (new) | 2 failed | 2 passed |

The new test empties FA4's combine cache, runs the warmup for a layer with 8 query heads over 1 KV head and for one with 16 over 2, then runs a split-KV decode over 8K keys. It checks that the decode ran the combine, so it can't pass without a split. On main the decode compiles a combine kernel for the layer's heads, and the test fails on it. The test skips off SM90, and `tests/v1/attention` runs in CI's H100 "V1 Attention" step. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, and so does its manual stage.

The requests in Claims ran in one process per model and build, with prefix caching on. Each process ran a fresh 32K-token prompt, then two prompts that add 64 new tokens to its first 32,704 tokens, then a second fresh 32K-token prompt. The script counts FA4's compile-cache keys around each request.

<details>
<summary>Why the 64-token requests split the keys, and the script</summary>

The prefix cache reuses whole KV blocks, so a request that adds 64 tokens schedules 128 tokens on E2B and 256 on 12B over about 32K cached keys. FA4 splits the keys of that step and runs the combine, and under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` such a prefill step runs outside a full CUDA graph.

```python
# First short-query-over-long-context request after startup, on stock Gemma 4:
# FA4 compile-cache keys and time to first token.
import os, random, time

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")  # keep the engine in-process
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, TokensPrompt

MODEL = "google/gemma-4-E2B-it"
llm = LLM(MODEL, max_model_len=32768 + 512, enable_prefix_caching=True, max_num_seqs=1,
          limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "audio": 0, "video": 0})
from vllm.vllm_flash_attn.cute.interface import _flash_attn_fwd, _flash_attn_fwd_combine

special = set(llm.get_tokenizer().all_special_ids)
vocab = [i for i in range(1000, 200000) if i not in special]
rng = random.Random(0)
fresh = lambda n: [rng.choice(vocab) for _ in range(n)]
params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0.0)
state = fresh(32704)
steps = [("fresh 32K prompt", state + fresh(64)),
         ("64 new tokens over the cached 32K", state + fresh(64)),
         ("64 new tokens over the cached 32K", state + fresh(64)),
         ("fresh 32K prompt", fresh(32768))]
for name, ids in steps:
    before = (len(_flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache.cache), len(_flash_attn_fwd_combine.compile_cache.cache))
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids)], params, use_tqdm=False)
    t = time.perf_counter() - t0
    after = (len(_flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache.cache), len(_flash_attn_fwd_combine.compile_cache.cache))
    print(f"{name}: {t:.3f} s, new forward kernels {after[0] - before[0]}, new combine kernels {after[1] - before[1]}")
```

</details>

## Details

The warmup is `FA4DenseAttentionKernel` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`, from #55768, registered for Gemma 4 checkpoints. FA4's `_flash_attn_fwd_combine` puts `out_partial.shape[-2]`, the number of heads, in its compile key. `FA4DenseAttentionKernel.compile` compiles the forward through `compile_flash_attn_varlen_func_from_specs`, which returns before FA4's SplitKV combine, and then calls `_flash_attn_fwd_combine` under `FakeTensorMode` to compile the combine for the 32, 64, 128 and 256 split buckets. That call passed `out_partial` of shape `(num_splits, 2, 1, 512)`, which is one head.

The warmup's compile key now records `num_qo_heads`, which `dispatch` already receives, and the combine is compiled with that many heads. Layers with the same query heads per KV head but a different number of heads now get separate keys.

The serving-time compile falls on a split-KV call outside a full CUDA graph at head size 512 on SM90, which on Gemma 4 means its full-attention layers. A step that schedules a few tokens over a long cached context makes such a call, for example a follow-up turn that hits the prefix cache. Decode steps under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` run the graphs captured at startup.

### Related work

#63279 and #64134 (open) change the same warmup's prefill specializations, but not the combine call. #65349 added the combine warmup for FA4's MLA path.

### Not covered

We did not run Blackwell (this combine is warmed only on SM90 at head size 512), other head sizes or eager mode.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Add __syncwarp before the lane-0 stores in the fused KDA decode block reductions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In `csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu`, the two pairwise block reductions let lane 0 of warp 0 overwrite `scratch[0]` and `scratch[1]` right after the warp reads the per-warp partials from the same buffer. Lane 1 reads `scratch[1]`, and nothing orders that read before lane 0's store. This PR adds one `__syncwarp()` before the stores in each function. TensorRT-LLM made the same change to the same two functions in its copy of this kernel ([NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19830](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19830)).

## Claims

- Removes an intra-warp shared-memory race in `block_reduce_sum2_for` and `block_reduce_sum2_active_for`. compute-sanitizer racecheck reports it on main and reports no hazards with this change.
- Outputs do not change: they are bitwise identical before and after on B200.
- No measurable latency change. The fix adds one `WARPSYNC` instruction per kernel.

## Validation

Setup: one B200, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0, compute-sanitizer 2025.3.1. vLLM at 3d81a51 with `_C_stable_libtorch` built from source (`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0`, Release), without and with this patch. The other extensions come from the precompiled wheel.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| racecheck on `test_fused_kda_decode_correctness` (command below) | 2400 warnings, 0 errors | 0 hazards |
| `test_fused_kda_decode_correctness`, native backend | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| `fused_kda_decode` outputs (`out`, `conv_state`, `state`), 12 parameter sets × 3 seeds | | bitwise identical to main, 36/36 |
| fused kernel latency, `benchmark_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py --graph` | | ratio to main 0.9999–1.0038 |

Commands, from the repo root:

```bash
# Test, both builds: 10 passed
python -m pytest -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py::test_fused_kda_decode_correctness -k native
# Reproducer: 2400 racecheck warnings on main, 0 with this PR
compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck --racecheck-report hazard \
  python -m pytest -q tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py::test_fused_kda_decode_correctness -k native
# Latency, three runs per build in alternating order
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py --graph --heads 12 24 48 96 --tokens 1 8 32 128
```

The output comparison is a short script that builds the test's inputs, calls `ops.fused_kda_decode` with each build, and compares the saved tensors byte by byte.

- **racecheck.** All 2400 warnings on main are `(Warp Level Programming) Potential WAR hazard` records in `kda_decode_fusion_many_heads_kernel`: read by thread (1,0,0), written by thread (0,0,0), at the 4 bytes of `scratch[1]` (`__shared__ 0x8e04`–`0x8e07`). That is one record per byte for each of the 600 CTAs in the 10 test cases. vLLM builds this file without `-lineinfo`. A standalone `-lineinfo` build of the same file attributes the pair to `block_reduce_sum2_for<8>`: the read of `scratch[lane]` at [L185](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d81a510f9ebc802a7864ced38832182295f4cad/csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu#L185) and the store `scratch[1] = block_y` at [L191](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d81a510f9ebc802a7864ced38832182295f4cad/csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu#L191).
- **SASS.** In that standalone build, this PR adds exactly 128 instructions over the 128 kernel instantiations, all `WARPSYNC`. The `BAR.SYNC` count is unchanged.
- **Latency.** The largest difference is +0.02 µs (for example 96 heads, 1 token: 5.27 → 5.29 µs). Per-configuration numbers are in the table below.
- **Verifier.** We found the race with a PTX-level synchronization and race verifier we are developing ([gpu-verifier/sentryward](https://github.com/gpu-verifier/sentryward)). On `kda_decode_fusion_many_heads_kernel` (12 heads, `sm_100f`, CUDA 13.2), it reports the same pair: `ld.shared.b32` by thread 1 and `st.shared.b32` by thread 0 on `scratch[1]`, with no happens-before order. With `bar.warp.sync -1` inserted before the stores, the result is `race_free`.
- **Tests.** No new test. The race does not change outputs, so a unit test cannot tell main from this PR; the racecheck run above is the reproducer, as in NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19830. The existing test runs in the `(B200) Kimi K3` CI step, which changes under `csrc/kimi_k3/` trigger.
- **Not run.** End-to-end serving and model evaluation: we have one B200. The kernel outputs are bitwise identical, so model outputs do not change.

<details>
<summary>Fused kernel latency per configuration (µs, median of 3 runs, [min–max])</summary>

| heads | tokens | main | this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 | 1 | 5.17 [5.15–5.17] | 5.17 [5.17–5.17] |
| 12 | 8 | 5.27 [5.27–5.27] | 5.29 [5.28–5.29] |
| 12 | 32 | 8.70 [8.70–8.70] | 8.70 [8.70–8.70] |
| 12 | 128 | 37.31 [37.30–37.33] | 37.31 [37.30–37.31] |
| 24 | 1 | 5.17 [5.17–5.17] | 5.17 [5.17–5.18] |
| 24 | 8 | 6.74 [6.74–6.74] | 6.74 [6.74–6.74] |
| 24 | 32 | 15.55 [15.55–15.56] | 15.55 [15.55–15.55] |
| 24 | 128 | 76.13 [76.10–76.15] | 76.12 [76.12–76.13] |
| 48 | 1 | 5.21 [5.20–5.21] | 5.23 [5.22–5.23] |
| 48 | 8 | 8.67 [8.67–8.67] | 8.67 [8.67–8.67] |
| 48 | 32 | 37.51 [37.50–37.52] | 37.51 [37.51–37.51] |
| 48 | 128 | 146.64 [146.64–146.70] | 146.67 [146.61–146.80] |
| 96 | 1 | 5.27 [5.27–5.27] | 5.29 [5.29–5.29] |
| 96 | 8 | 15.57 [15.57–15.57] | 15.57 [15.57–15.57] |
| 96 | 32 | 75.66 [75.63–75.68] | 75.66 [75.66–75.68] |
| 96 | 128 | 289.90 [289.82–290.36] | 290.00 [289.91–290.02] |

</details>

## Details

`block_reduce_sum2_for` ([L168–L196](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d81a510f9ebc802a7864ced38832182295f4cad/csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu#L168-L196)) on main (3d81a51):

```
if (warp == 0) {
  block_x = lane < kReduceWarps ? scratch[lane] : 0.0f;                 // lane 1 reads scratch[1]
  block_y = lane < kReduceWarps ? scratch[kReduceWarps + lane] : 0.0f;
  block_x = warp_reduce_sum(block_x);                                   // __shfl_xor_sync only
  block_y = warp_reduce_sum(block_y);
  if (lane == 0) {
    scratch[0] = block_x;
    scratch[1] = block_y;                                               // lane 0 writes scratch[1]
  }
}
```

- Root cause: the `__syncthreads()` before this block orders the per-warp writes before these reads, and the one after orders the final stores before every thread reads the result. Nothing orders lane 1's read of `scratch[1]` before lane 0's store to it. Shuffles do not order shared-memory accesses.
- Why outputs are correct today: lane 0's totals depend on lane 1's loaded value through the shuffles, so in practice the load returns before the store. That is a data dependency, not an order the CUDA memory model guarantees; `__syncwarp()` provides the order.
- `block_reduce_sum2_active_for` ([L230–L262](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3d81a510f9ebc802a7864ced38832182295f4cad/csrc/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel.cu#L230-L262)) has the same sequence. The current launcher instantiates only `block_reduce_sum2_for`. The patch fixes both, so the active variant stays correct if it is enabled.
- The single-value reductions (`block_reduce_sum`, `block_reduce_sum_active_for`) do not have this problem: lane 0 writes only `scratch[0]`, which only lane 0 reads. The ROCm copy (`fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`) does not have this pattern either: its `block_reduce_sum3` stores the totals at `scratch[3 * kGroups]` and after, past the partials that the lanes read.
- Base: the branch is rebased onto main 28dd9c3 (2026-11-02). `csrc/kimi_k3/` is unchanged between 3d81a51, where we ran the validation above, and 28dd9c3.
- Duplicate check: no open PR touches this file. We searched open PRs and issues for `fused_kda_decode`, `syncwarp` and `kda race`.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Use AITER Triton bf16 BMM for the decode W_UV when tuned
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, run the MLA decode W_UV up-projection (`MLAAttention._v_up_proj`) on AITER's Triton bf16 batched GEMM when AITER has a tuned config for the layer's exact shape; otherwise keep `torch.bmm`. With the Kimi-K2.6 config from ROCm/aiter#6780 this speeds up Kimi-K2 / K2.5 / K2.6 decode at TP8 on MI355X.

All numbers below were measured with #61863 (now merged) applied to both the baseline and this PR; without it, Kimi-K2.6 takes the FP8 MLA prefill path, which produced wrong output (GSM8K 0.027 vs 0.93).

Requires AITER with ROCm/aiter#6780 (merged `c617bd42f2`, included in v0.1.27; the vLLM image bump is #63774).

## Claims

- Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4, TP8, MI355X: the decode W_UV GEMM drops from 9.1 µs to 5.0 µs per layer (hipBLASLt → AITER Triton), about 260 µs per decode step at 64 tokens.
- Serving: mean TPOT −3.0% at 1k/1k c=16, −2.2% at c=128 and −2.3% at 1k/8k c=64; at 1k/1k c=64, −3.4% with 256 prompts and +0.3% with 640 prompts.
- Same bf16 weights and math as `torch.bmm`; GSM8K and GPQA Diamond are unchanged within stderr.
- Only the W_UV kernel changes. Shapes AITER has no tuned config for keep `torch.bmm`.

## Validation

Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X (gfx950), AITER at `c617bd42f2`, ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`.

**Serving** (`vllm bench serve`, random, seed 0; 10 × concurrency prompts except where noted; this PR measured on a second pass of the same server, so Triton kernels are already compiled):

| ISL/OSL, conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean E2EL (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k, 16 | 1,597 → 1,622 (+1.5%) | 9.75 → 9.46 (−3.0%) | 10.26 → 10.10 (−1.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 64 (256 prompts) | 4,124 → 4,275 (+3.6%) | 14.71 → 14.21 (−3.4%) | 15.88 → 15.32 (−3.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 64 (640 prompts) | 4,256 → 4,234 (−0.5%) | 14.42 → 14.47 (+0.3%) | 15.40 → 15.47 (+0.5%) |
| 1k/1k, 128 | 6,372 → 6,507 (+2.1%) | 19.34 → 18.92 (−2.2%) | 20.56 → 20.14 (−2.1%) |
| 1k/8k, 64 | 4,032 → 4,128 (+2.4%) | 15.79 → 15.43 (−2.3%) | 130.0 → 127.0 (−2.3%) |

`vllm bench serve --model /data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len <1024|8192> --max-concurrency <c> --num-prompts <10*c> --ignore-eos --seed 0`

**Accuracy** (lm-eval):

| Task | Filter | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K, 5-shot | flexible-extract | 0.9386 ± 0.0066 | 0.9416 ± 0.0065 |
| GSM8K, 5-shot | strict-match | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | 0.9424 ± 0.0064 |
| GPQA Diamond CoT, 0-shot | flexible-extract | 0.7172 ± 0.0321 | 0.6818 ± 0.0332 |

GPQA strict-match is ~0.05 in both runs because its answer format doesn't match Kimi-K2.6's output, so it is omitted. The GPQA difference (−3.5 points, 7 of 198 questions) is within one standard error of the difference (~0.046).

**Kernel swap.** In rank-0 profiler traces of both versions, every step type that runs MLA decode changes only its 61 W_UV kernels per step (one per layer). W_UK and all other kernels are unchanged, and pure-prefill steps are kernel-for-kernel identical.

<details>
<summary>Per step type</summary>

| Step type | Before (hipBLASLt) | After (AITER Triton) | Per call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode, 64 tokens | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x64x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 16×32×256 (`M_LEQ_64`) | 9.14 → 4.97 µs |
| Decode, 32 tokens | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 16×32×256 (`M_LEQ_32`) | 8.00 → 4.53 µs |
| Decode, 1 token | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 32×32×256 (`M_LEQ_8`) | 7.03 → 4.23 µs |
| Prefill 32,767 + 1 decode token | `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS…MT128x32x128` | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` 32×32×256 (`M_LEQ_8`) | 9.64 → 4.06 µs |
| Prefill, 1,024 tokens | unchanged | unchanged | — |

</details>

**Tests**
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -v -k "v_up_proj or post_load"` on MI355X: `passed`
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports, torch.cuda and test-tethering checks pass.

## Details

- **Dispatch rule.** `rocm_aiter_ops.is_triton_bf16_bmm_tuned(B, M, N, K)` asks AITER's config lookup whether the exact shape has a tuned entry on the current GPU (cached per shape). It reuses `_triton_gemm_config_is_tuned`, which now takes optional `M` and `B`, and follows `is_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned`. There is no env var or model check; FP4/FP8 BMM still take precedence.
- **Scope with ROCm/aiter#6780.** The config is keyed on 8 heads (`B=8-N=128-K=512`), so it applies to the Kimi-K2 family at TP8, and to DeepSeek-V3 at TP16, which has the same per-GPU shape. AITER's lookup never reports an `any` entry as tuned, so the 16,384-token `any` config is not used: above 128 decode tokens W_UV stays on `torch.bmm`.
- **Safety.** `_v_up_proj` runs inside the MLA attention custom op, so torch.compile doesn't trace into the Triton call, and CUDA graphs capture it per batch size. It uses vLLM's existing strided views; there are no copies or weight changes.
- **Test.** `test_mla_v_up_proj_runs_tuned_aiter_triton_bf16_bmm` (ROCm only) uses a shape AITER already ships tuned gfx942/gfx950 configs for (N=1024, K=4096), so the real tuned lookup passes in CI without patching. It checks via the profiler that the AITER kernel ran, and compares against the `torch.bmm` path it replaces. Kimi's own shape needs the new AITER config, which the CI image may not have yet; it was validated on MI355X as above. The test reuses the existing hand-built `MLAAttention` setup in `test_mla_backends.py` (now a shared `_bare_mla_layer` helper) and runs in the MI355 V1 Attention step.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs searched for `batched_gemm_bf16`, `_v_up_proj` and AITER bf16 BMM: #53003 and #61926 use AITER's `batched_gemm_bf16` for DeepSeek-V4's einsum (a different call site); #36297 and #59856 fuse FP8 output quantization into `_v_up_proj`; #55741 refactors MLA BMM selection into an `MLABmm` abstraction without a Triton bf16 path. This change would fit #55741 as one more implementation.
- **Limitation.** "Tuned in AITER" is taken to mean faster than hipBLASLt. AITER's tuner compares Triton configs against each other, not against `torch.bmm`; for this shape it holds in every bucket exercised above.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the implementation, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.
