commits.pr_title: [KV Cache] Allow mixed page sizes in a layer-compact KV layout (for Nemotron Shortcut)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Nemotron Shortcut ([#68198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68198)) needs a layer-compact KV cache layout with mixed page sizes. Its SDSA indexer cache joins its core's KV cache group, so that group mixes page sizes, and the SDSA core supports only `LBHNC`. `validate_kv_cache_layout` refuses this today, although `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places it correctly. This PR relaxes the check. No model on `main` hits it.

No other model is affected: the check only got looser and the placement order did not change, so every configuration accepted on `main` is accepted with the same layout.

Why layer-outer, when Kimi-K3 and Qwen4-exp, which also mix linear-attention layers with an indexer cache, use block-outer packing: the SDSA core reads each layer's pages as one pool of token rows, so the layer dim must stay outermost with dense pages. Block-outer packing would also put the model under NIXL's limits for packed layouts (the pull connector refuses them with PP, and PP push needs MLA).

## Claims

- A model with more than one KV cache group and mixed page sizes can use a layer-compact layout (`LBHNC`, `LBNHC`) when the layers that overlay each other have the same block stride. Groupings whose overlaid layers differ are still refused with the same error; single-group models, uniform page sizes and block-outer layouts behave as before.

## Validation

**Reproducer** (CPU only):

<details><summary>repro_kv_layout.py</summary>

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import torch

from vllm.config import CacheConfig
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import get_kv_cache_config_from_groups
from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import FullAttentionManager
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheGroup, MLAAttentionSpec


def spec(head_size: int) -> MLAAttentionSpec:
    return MLAAttentionSpec(
        block_size=64, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=head_size, dtype=torch.uint8
    )


def group(specs: dict) -> KVCacheGroup:
    return KVCacheGroup.from_layers(
        {name: FullAttentionManager.layer_config(s) for name, s in specs.items()}
    )


# Group 0: 3 attention layers (32 KiB pages), then 3 indexer caches (8 KiB pages).
# Group 1: 3 sliding-window-style layers (32 KiB pages).
attn = {f"attn.{i}": spec(512) for i in range(3)}
indexer = {f"indexer.{i}": spec(128) for i in range(3)}
swa = {f"swa.{i}": spec(512) for i in range(3)}
groups = [group(attn | indexer), group(swa)]

vllm_config = MagicMock()
vllm_config.cache_config = CacheConfig()
vllm_config.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks_override = None
vllm_config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = "LBHNC"
vllm_config.attention_config.hisparse_config = None
config = get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(vllm_config, groups, 64 << 20)
for tensor in config.kv_cache_tensors:
    print(tensor.layers, "offset", tensor.offset, "block_stride", tensor.block_stride)
```

</details>

On `main`:

```
ValueError: KV cache layout LBHNC cannot express this model's mixed page sizes ([8192, 32768]); a backend should declare block-outermost supported layouts (e.g. BLHNC), or set VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC.
```

With this PR, the sliding-window-style layers overlay the attention layers, and the indexer caches get regions of their own after them:

```
['attn.0', 'attn.1', 'attn.2'] offset 0 block_stride 32768
['indexer.0', 'indexer.1', 'indexer.2'] offset 53673984 block_stride 8192
['swa.0', 'swa.1', 'swa.2'] offset 0 block_stride 32768
```

**Unit tests with this PR** (one node of 4x GB300, torch 2.14):

`pytest tests/v1/core`, on `main` `26acafd`: **1331 passed, 1 failed** (26 min). The failure, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short[True]`, fails the same way on `main` without this PR:

```
AssertionError: assert 'gpu_memory_utilization' in '--max-model-len auto reduced max_model_len from 256 to 128 (0.0 GiB GPU left for the KV cache after CUDA graph capture and warmup). ...'
```

**pre-commit** on the changed files: ruff, typos, mypy and the repo's own checks pass (the markdown, shell, GitHub Actions, C++, Rust and requirements hooks were skipped: no such files changed).

## Details

In a layer-compact layout, `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` gives each layer of a group a region of its own; every group's regions start at byte 0 and follow one another, so the i-th layer of one group shares its region with the i-th layer of every other group. A block belongs to one group at a time, so this overlay is correct whenever the layers sharing a region have the same block stride, whatever the page sizes of the other layers:

```
block strides P and p
group 0: [P, P, p, p]   group 1: [P, P]      overlaid layers match: placed correctly, but refused on main
group 0: [P, P, p, p]   group 1: [P, P, P]   region 2 is p in one group and P in the other: refused
```

`validate_kv_cache_layout` refused every multi-group model with mixed page sizes under a layer-compact layout. It now refuses only when overlaid layers differ (`_overlaid_layers_match`). One helper, `_group_layers_by_spec`, gives the region order to the check and to both placements (`get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` and HiSparse's `_build_hisparse_kv_cache_tensors`), so they cannot drift.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Select full-warp top-k rows with redux.sync and keep selections in registers (SM80+)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`topkGating` (`csrc/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu`) gives each row to one full warp when the row is wide enough (512 experts, 256 experts with 16-bit logits, 128-512 experts with fp32 logits). For each of the k selections it runs a 5-stage shuffle butterfly with 3 dependent shuffles per stage, then lane 0 stores the selection and later re-reads the weights to scale them.

For those rows, without a correction bias, this PR selects each expert with two `redux.sync` reductions (`__reduce_max_sync` on the score key, then `__reduce_min_sync` on the expert among the lanes that hold the max), keeps selection i in the registers of lane i, rescans only in the winning lane, and writes the row once at the end. The output is bitwise equal to `main`: the same experts, the same order, the same lowest-index tie rule and the same weight bits.

The register-resident output path is from @Gin-Sin (#64731, co-author); the SM80+ `redux.sync` selection scope is from this PR. #64731 will be closed in favour of this PR.

## Claims

- **Same output:** bitwise equal to `main` (ids, weights as bits, token-expert indices) in every case run on A100, including tie-heavy, all-equal and NaN/Inf rows.
- **Faster on SM80+:** E 512 top-10 softmax on A100: 0.59-0.68x of `main`'s time at 1-256 tokens, 0.71-0.76x at 1,024-4,096 tokens. On B300 (measured by @Gin-Sin): 1.7-2.7x faster than `main` at every full-warp shape.
- **End to end:** below serving noise. On B300 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, DP4 + EP, MTP 3, with the #64731 output path) throughput changed by at most about 1 %, inside the main-vs-main spread; GSM8K and greedy outputs are unchanged. Against `main`, the kernel saves 2.7-4.7 us per router call on A100 (1-256 tokens) and 2.5-6.9 us on B300 (E 512, 1-464 tokens).
- **No change elsewhere:** biased routing, k > 32, sub-warp rows (for example E 128 with 16-bit logits), ROCm and pre-SM80 GPUs keep the current loop, which is byte-identical to `main`. No new CPU/GPU sync, no new launch, no change to the op schema.

## Validation

**Kernel A/B, one A100-SXM4-40GB (sm_80), 31 Oct 2026.** Four copies of `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` are built side by side as separate `torch.utils.cpp_extension` modules (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80`): `main` 17550580e9, the first revision of this PR c7f8f96ee8, #64731 7a51d76027, and this PR c752616c1d. Each time is per call under CUDA graph replay (100 calls x 20 replays, minimum of 3 interleaved rounds). E 512, top-10, softmax, renormalize.

| logits | tokens | main | first revision | #64731 | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fp32 | 1 | 9.99 us | 7.69 us | 6.48 us | **5.31 us** |
| fp32 | 8 | 8.35 us | 6.36 us | 5.77 us | **5.34 us** |
| fp32 | 64 | 8.69 us | 6.71 us | 5.69 us | **5.37 us** |
| fp32 | 256 | 9.01 us | 7.12 us | 5.85 us | **5.38 us** |
| fp32 | 1,024 | 11.84 us | 10.90 us | 9.17 us | **8.71 us** |
| fp32 | 4,096 | 26.54 us | 25.54 us | 21.60 us | **20.25 us** |
| bf16 | 1 | 7.79 us | 5.85 us | 5.45 us | **5.02 us** |
| bf16 | 8 | 8.56 us | 6.62 us | 5.76 us | **5.33 us** |
| bf16 | 64 | 8.67 us | 6.73 us | 5.72 us | **5.24 us** |
| bf16 | 256 | 9.00 us | 7.05 us | 5.76 us | **5.38 us** |
| bf16 | 1,024 | 11.74 us | 10.76 us | 9.03 us | **8.35 us** |
| bf16 | 4,096 | 26.35 us | 25.37 us | 21.47 us | **19.98 us** |

Bitwise checks against `main` on the same A100: every timed case above, plus 36 tie-heavy cases (fp32 / bf16 / fp16 x tokens 1 / 7 / 64 / 333 x few distinct values / all-equal rows / wide randn): 0 mismatches for all three changed copies. 

**B300 (sm_100), measured by @Gin-Sin on this head c752616c1d** ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62912#issuecomment-6541421469)): CUDA 13.1, FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph and cold L2, median of 3 rotated rounds; bitwise equal to `main` in 336/336 case-runs.

| logits | E / top-k | tokens | main | #64731 | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 1 | 6.50 us | 4.00 us | **3.78 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 64 | 8.86 us | 3.97 us | **3.74 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 464 | 11.04 us | 4.32 us | **4.10 us** |
| bf16 | 512 / 10 | 8,192 | 32.96 us | 19.90 us | **18.62 us** |
| fp32 | 256 / 8 | 64 | 7.78 us | 3.36 us | **3.17 us** |
| bf16 | 128 / 8 (sub-warp, unchanged path) | 64 | 6.24 us | 6.24 us | 6.24 us |

End-to-end serving and GSM8K on B300 with the #64731 output path are in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62912#issuecomment-6536962624): no difference beyond run-to-run noise at concurrency 16/64, about +1 % at 464 (at the edge of noise); GSM8K 0.967/0.969 (main) vs 0.971/0.969; greedy outputs identical on 200/200 prompts.

## Details

**Why it is exact.** Without a bias the choice score is the output score. After softmax or sigmoid and the existing NaN/Inf clamp every score is >= +0, so the unsigned order of the float bits is the float order. Each lane offers `key = score bits + 1` for its best unselected slot (a selected slot has key 0). The first `redux.sync` finds the maximum key; the second finds the minimum expert among lanes that hold it, which is the lowest expert index, the same tie rule as the butterfly. Only the owner lane clears its slot and rescans. Lane i keeps selection i; lanes 0..k-1 write once at the end, with the same fp32 renormalization sum order and the same scale as `main`.

**Scope.** `topkGating` rows with `THREADS_PER_ROW == WARP_SIZE`, no bias, k <= 32, `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800`, not ROCm; the launcher picks a separate `FULL_WARP_SELECT` instantiation, so the existing loop's code generation does not change. Rows beyond `num_rows` return per warp before the selection, so all 32 lanes reach each `redux.sync`. TensorRT-LLM uses `redux.sync` for this selection on SM100+.

**Tests.** `test_topk_without_bias_matches_zero_bias` (from #64731, extended) compares a launch without a bias against a launch with an all-zero bias, which keeps the old loop, bit for bit: E 128/352/384/512/576, k 1/10/32, bf16/fp16/fp32, softmax/sigmoid, renormalize on/off, `is_padding` rows, `routed_scaling_factor`, tie-heavy rows with NaN/+Inf, and the tie order against a stable sort (720 cases). **Full build run (11 Nov 2026, head 4dcef2dbf7, rebased on `main` 960f5c1bb1; the current head ea58a25789 has the same kernel and test and only drops a benchmark option):** in-tree CMake build of `_C_stable_libtorch` and `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` on an 8 x A100-SXM4-40GB node (nightly cu130 image: CUDA 13.0, g++ 13.3, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0`), once from `main` 960f5c1bb1 and once with this PR's source file. The node has no network, so the CUTLASS headers are the 4.5.0 copy shipped with FlashInfer instead of the pinned v4.7.1 (only `scaled_mm_c2x` uses them), and the externally fetched projects (triton_kernels, DeepGEMM, FlashMLA and the others) are not rebuilt; their libraries come from the image. `tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py` on one A100: **this PR 1,588 passed; `main` 868 passed; this PR's tests on the `main` build 1,588 passed** (expected: the output is bitwise equal, so the new cases also pass on the old loop).

**CI.** There is no sm_80 runner. The A100 data come from our cluster.

**Related.** #64731 (Gin-Sin, same selection; its output path is folded in here). #59737 (PDL for this kernel, SM90+ only) does not overlap. #57823 (padded row strides) touches the same file.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview Inkling 2 on Hopper: replace the Triton expert GEMMs (`moe_sm90.bmm`, added in #67880) with Humming's indexed MoE GEMMs (NVFP4 / MXFP8 weights, bf16 activations). Follow-up to #67880; no other open PR touches the Inkling 2 Hopper MoE. ## Claims - Inkling-2-Small NVFP4, TP4 on H200: serving output throughput **1.48x** at concurrency 1 and **2.71x** at concurrency 64 (`vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out); GSM8K unchanged (0.976 → 0.976). - Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8, TP8 on H200: **1.13x** at concurrency 1 and **2.06x** at concurrency 64; GSM8K 0.976 → 0.974. - Forward step (`vllm bench forward`, NVFP4 TP4): decode 1.23–1.45x faster, 2k prefill 1.87x faster. - Deterministic: Humming's stream-K is disabled (it adds K slices into the output with bf16 `atomicAdd`); graph vs. eager and eager vs. eager are bitwise equal in every case. - Blackwell is unchanged. ## Validation All on 8x H200, precompiled wheel of `main` cc5dafc136 for both sides; `main` = cc5dafc136, PR = 21957ec79b. **Tests** (H200, PR 21957ec79b): ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/inkling2 -q 164 passed, 38 skipped, 17 warnings in 443.61s (0:07:23) ``` New / modified MoE tests (`-k "humming_experts_are_deterministic or select_experts_matches_torch or moe_layer_matches_reference or expert_parallel or padding_tokens" --durations=0`): `25 passed, 33 deselected in 39.93s`; the slowest is `test_humming_experts_are_deterministic[1-nvfp4]` at 5.98s. With the stream-K override removed, `test_humming_experts_are_deterministic` fails in 3 of its 4 cases (`3 failed, 1 passed`). **Accuracy and serving.** Server and eval commands (same for `main` and the PR): ```bash vllm serve --served-model-name inkling2 --tokenizer-mode inkling -tp <4|8> \ --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 4096 --temperature 0 \ --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 128 vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model inkling2 --tokenizer --tokenizer-mode inkling \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos \ --num-prompts <16|512> --max-concurrency <1|64> --seed 0 ``` | | GSM8K | conc. 1 tok/s (TPOT) | conc. 64 tok/s (TPOT) | |---|---|---|---| | NVFP4 TP4, main | 0.976 | 110.9 (8.53 ms) | 708.7 (79.08 ms) | | NVFP4 TP4, PR | 0.976 | 164.3 (5.79 ms) | 1918.6 (29.93 ms) | | MXFP8 TP8, main | 0.976 | 152.0 (6.26 ms) | 1279.3 (42.82 ms) | | MXFP8 TP8, PR | 0.974 | 172.5 (5.55 ms) | 2633.9 (22.18 ms) | GSM8K invalid responses were 0.000 in all four runs.
Raw vllm bench serve output, NVFP4 TP4, concurrency 64 main: ``` Successful requests: 512 Benchmark duration (s): 184.95 Output token throughput (tok/s): 708.70 Total token throughput (tok/s): 3543.51 Mean TTFT (ms): 2937.22 Median TTFT (ms): 1534.64 P99 TTFT (ms): 16269.66 Mean TPOT (ms): 79.08 Median TPOT (ms): 71.51 P99 TPOT (ms): 132.08 ``` PR: ``` Successful requests: 512 Benchmark duration (s): 68.32 Output token throughput (tok/s): 1918.58 Total token throughput (tok/s): 9592.91 Mean TTFT (ms): 897.09 Median TTFT (ms): 784.41 P99 TTFT (ms): 3233.31 Mean TPOT (ms): 29.93 Median TPOT (ms): 30.12 P99 TPOT (ms): 33.52 ```
**Forward step**, NVFP4 TP4 (`--load-format auto --routing real --kv-len-jitter 0`): ```bash torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward --model Inkling-2-Small -tp 4 \ --load-format auto --routing real --kv-len-jitter 0 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 128 --case decode_bs1=1*1@4096 --case decode_bs8=8*1@4096 --case decode_bs32=32*1@4096 \ --case decode_bs128=128*1@4096 --case prefill_2k=2048 ``` | case | main | PR | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | decode_bs1 | 8568.9 us | 5922.7 us | 1.45x | | decode_bs8 | 9635.8 us | 7720.6 us | 1.25x | | decode_bs32 | 14860.1 us | 11457.7 us | 1.30x | | decode_bs128 | 32949.9 us | 26737.9 us | 1.23x | | prefill_2k | 173674.5 us | 92716.0 us | 1.87x | Sample spread ≤ 0.29%; `graph vs eager rel rms 0.0e+00` in every case on both sides. ## Details - **Why Humming.** The Triton GEMM dequantizes weights in registers and reaches only 0.6–0.9 TB/s of weight bandwidth at decode for NVFP4. Humming's W4A16 / W8A16 kernels run 1.4–2.6x faster per GEMM at 1–32 tokens on these shapes. `humming-kernels` is already a CUDA requirement (`requirements/cuda.txt`). Marlin MoE could not be compared: the precompiled `_moe_C` has no SM90 image that loads on this driver. - **Hopper path** (`ops/moe_sm90.py`): - **Routing:** `select_experts` reuses the router helpers of `ops.moe.route` (`_select_experts`, `_local_experts`) and writes only the local expert ids, routing weights and an identity `src2dst`. Hopper no longer builds the tile-padded layout or quantizes activations. - **GEMMs:** after loading, `HummingExperts` repacks the checkpoint tensors with Humming's modelopt NVFP4 / MXFP8 schemas. The NVFP4 global scale is `amax / outer_scale_denominator` per expert. It frees the originals and runs two `indexed` GEMMs. - **Glue:** `moe_align_block_size` sorts the rows; a bf16 kernel applies the softcapped SwiGLU (reusing `activation._situ`); `ops.moe.combine` sums the rows unchanged. The all-reduce and sequence-parallel push are unchanged too. - **Why not `HummingIndexedExperts`.** Inkling 2's experts are not a `FusedMoE`: they own routing, EP sharding and the combine. So this calls the `vllm.utils.humming` facade directly instead of going through the modular kernel. - **Determinism.** Humming's heuristic configs enable stream-K for some row ranges (e.g. few rows of large experts under EP, and ≥ ~1000 rows). Its epilogue adds K slices into the bf16 output with `atomicAdd`, which made eager-vs-eager outputs differ. - We set `use_stream_k = False` in every config. Batch invariance is still opt-in via `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. - Cost: at 1 token per rank on TP4 (about 2 local rows), the expert GEMMs take about 15 µs per layer longer than with stream-K. The end-to-end decode above includes this. - **Numerics.** Weights are dequantized exactly. Activations stay in bf16 instead of being quantized to NVFP4 / MXFP8 as on Blackwell, so Hopper no longer matches Blackwell bitwise. - On Hopper, the MoE reference test keeps activations in bf16. - The tile-layout tests (`test_bmm_matches_dequantized_matmul`, `test_token_tiles_match`) now run on Blackwell only. - **Limitations.** - On Hopper, `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` (and their scales) are emptied after loading. Reloading weights in place would need to repack them again. - Expert LoRA remains unsupported, as before. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Release cached queries when Flash scoring is cancelled
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make Flash late-interaction cleanup resilient to repeated cancellation, with bounded waits for producer shutdown and query-cache release.

## Claims

- On failure, cancel query/document producers and give them up to 10 seconds to stop before attempting abort and cache release.
- Defer cancellation during cleanup without resetting the deadline, then re-raise it. The release RPC also has its own 10-second timeout.
- Preserve the existing request-error conversion and keep iterator merging on the regular pooling path.

## Validation

Retested on November 18:

- PR: `5ab1f7e9c44a1557cc0097ede78dbbd11c6cc9cc`.
- Comparison baseline: `f3f0a014240e1e0a778728f90469cba8d15ed1bb`, the main revision used for the November 17 rebase.
- Relevant CPU tests: **101 passed, 2 skipped, 2 deselected**. Pre-commit passed on all three changed files, including mypy.
- The same controlled regression cases still expose three failures on the baseline: an active producer, a pending document, and a cached query. They are included in the passing PR suite.

These unit cases deliberately control cancellation timing. I still haven't found a stable end-to-end HTTP reproducer of that race.

A10 HTTP smoke passed on both revisions, including score/rerank recovery after the expected admission rejection. The official `/rerank` benchmark completed **1,600 measured HTTP requests with zero errors**.

Each variant ran twice, with 200 measured requests per concurrency setting (1 and 8), 20 warmups per setting, and eight documents per request. The table shows run-level medians and the range of the two runs:

| Concurrency | Main HTTP req/s: median [range] | PR HTTP req/s: median [range] | Median difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 38.08 [37.35–38.82] | 37.94 [37.42–38.46] | -0.38% |
| 8 | 172.86 [168.06–177.66] | 172.51 [165.69–179.33] | -0.20% |

The paired changes went in both directions and the repeated-run ranges overlap. This small comparison did not show a consistent performance regression. Measured intervals were about 5.2–5.4 seconds at concurrency 1 and 1.1–1.2 seconds at concurrency 8; two short runs cannot establish a general performance guarantee.


<details>
<summary>CPU commands and recorded output</summary>

### Environment

The runs used the PR checkout's existing `.venv` on macOS/CPU. Read-only inspection of that interpreter on November 18 reported:

```python
"""Run pytest with an explicit source tree and audit every imported vLLM module."""

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys

source = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
report = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
os.chdir(source)
sys.path.insert(0, str(source))
os.environ.update(
    VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE="cpu",
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1",
    HF_HUB_OFFLINE="1",
    TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE="1",
)

import pytest

result = pytest.main([
    "--noconftest", "-q", "--tb=short", "-p", "no:cacheprovider",
    "-c", str(source / "pyproject.toml"), *sys.argv[3:],
])
paths = {
    name: str(Path(module.__file__).resolve())
    for name, module in tuple(sys.modules.items())
    if (name == "vllm" or name.startswith("vllm."))
    and getattr(module, "__file__", None)
}
unexpected = {name: path for name, path in paths.items()
              if not Path(path).is_relative_to(source / "vllm")}
report.write_text(json.dumps({
    "source": str(source), "pytest_exit_code": int(result),
    "module_count": len(paths), "unexpected_modules": unexpected,
    "module_paths": paths,
}, indent=2) + "\n")
raise SystemExit(99 if unexpected else result)
```

## Details

`merge_async_iterators()` cancels pending iterator tasks without joining them. The Flash path now owns its producer tasks so it can cancel and wait for them before attempting abort and query-cache release. Ordinary pooling still uses the existing merged iterator.

Cleanup is best effort. The limits apply to individual stages, not the whole request, and do not guarantee that remote cleanup has completed. If abort hits the outer deadline, its `finally` block can still attempt release within the separate RPC timeout after the handler stops waiting.
